how: The initiating post asks the room to get together and make a White Bear logo.
Members offer a shared design, resize it, propose an array, and later reconsider a larger single logo.
Reports describe laid tiles being covered and a wall of symbols forming, establishing construction and reporting without independently verifying the canvas.
A measured common image, smaller variant, and edited location answer make the proposed work findable while its scale remains open.
Members defend and offer maintenance of existing logos, while the added mechanism of keepers reversing an agreed redesign remains untested.
A participant distinguishes contacted vandals who reportedly stopped from continuing random purple placers.
Members urge restraint toward neighbouring art, repair of their damage, rainbow-preserving outlines, and direct appeals asking vandals to stop.
Internal accommodation proposals and reported contact with vandals do not establish bilateral borders, truces, or deals.
A single post calls for converting the Tesla sign into a White Bear feature, with enactment unresolved.
A member recounts restarting logos around other lettering and in a corner after disappearance and repeated overwriting.
Members claim a final pixel or logo and identify their contribution to surviving work after closure.
The surviving-logo celebration receives recollections of shared effort and enjoyment despite loss.
A member cheers unexpectedly good progress before the work has been declared complete.
A retrospective account records purple damage, repair, disappearance, rebuilding, and the final stop.
A wish for another event receives a successor-canvas referral, fitting hoped-for continuation without establishing collective adoption or uptake.
Maintenance offers and private-message reports leave the use of scripts or spare accounts undecided.
The direct reply to a wall-of-symbols help call reports doing a part without asking for anything back.
A fake release announcement is exposed, improved as bait, greeted, played along with, and admitted to have fooled a reader.
Members explicitly doubt whether their numbers and influence can sustain the intended work.
Provisional plans neither establish exhaustive local ordering practices nor test the model's cross-room frequency claim.
The member proposing the White Bear mark supplies the initiating role independently of subsequent participants' answers.
Messaging vandals does not establish a representative carrying the room's terms between rooms.
Urging repair of damage to a neighbour and requesting defenders do not establish traded inter-room help.
A statement about combining drawings does not establish a coalition or mutual-defence agreement.
A blue-corner challenge receives a reply about the area's earlier colour, supporting a minimal participant exchange without proving an inter-room campaign.
The conversion proposal names a target without identifying a quarrel carried into the canvas from earlier life.
The further defence post establishes canvas discussion but no moderator boundary, flood objection, or posting-rule change.
A participant explicitly links sustained attention to the build to its depiction of a favourite episode.
Proposed rainbow-compatible outlines do not establish a host granting space or governing guests' permission.
The Tesla conversion call supplies no pre-canvas tie explaining its target, while familiar show phrases establish no inherited rival.
Continuing random placement after private contact states no limit of representation, disclaimer of standing, or request for a negotiating leader.
Authorship claims and recollections of earlier loss do not establish a corrected attribution, cleanup dispute, or contest over the retained history.
A shared image and messages asking vandals to stop do not establish planning moving into a chat.
A participant asks whether the effort is progressing, with no answer beneath that question in the supplied forest.
A recruitment-sign proposal and an offer from someone new to the show do not establish an arrival caused by the canvas.
Members joke about organising six people, imagine multiplying tiny logos, and wonder whether the work resembles Space Invaders.
Initial reuse of existing black space saves background work, and a later quiet patch is chosen in anticipation of attracting little attention.
The quiet-patch choice follows reported tile loss yet anticipates avoiding attention, so prospective selection is not confined to the period before the room's first loss.
The existing fandom's build proposals and jokes supply no evidence of a new room forming around the canvas mark.
The coded canvas jokes do not establish objections to offensive words, slurs, or hate symbols.
An inscription proposal and a company-logo target do not establish outreach seeking notice from creators, companies, or press.
The colour exchange and practical restraint warning do not establish an exchange debating the general fairness of covering others' work.
Questions about progress and numerical doubt do not establish stress-driven withdrawal or an interpersonal quarrel repaired by other members.
Private messages ask vandals to stop, supplying no evidence of concealed strategy, coded language, or infiltration of a rival venue.
Numerical scepticism and reported vandalism do not establish members attacking their own work because they object to canvas posts.
A participant explains joining through spare time on a rainy Saturday.
The retrospective account locates repair late at night and reports discovering loss after waking, without establishing that sleep caused that loss.
A tile notification is followed by inability to access the site and recognition of closure, establishing a reported site limit without diagnosing an earlier fault.
The blue-corner exchange supplies no statement that a participant belongs to both communities or feels torn between them.
An explicit agreement to start the logo answers the initiating request to build it together.
The proposal supplies the target of its simultaneous first invitation, and a later wall report recruits around the same mark.
A member explicitly explains that purple changes to existing logos prompted attempts to fix them.
Defence and private contact occur, but no recorded passage establishes a turn into negotiating borders.
Restraint is explicit but an established agreement is unavailable for testing the border-to-restraint mechanism.
Visible maintenance pressure supplies no evidence deciding whether it led to scripts or spare accounts.
Unexpected progress can already prompt celebration while construction continues, so a prior declaration of completion is not required locally.
The surviving-logo celebration receives a direct authorship claim and a retrospective account of damage, loss, rebuilding, and closure.
A recollection ending in a wish for another event receives a successor-canvas referral, without establishing uptake.
Members can discuss enlargement while struggling to maintain existing work, so numerical shortage alone does not demonstrate cessation of defence and a move.
A measured design is a provisional common goal, while claiming settlement requires demonstrated adoption because competing scale proposals continue.
A direct bare contribution report answers the wall-of-symbols help call, while other joining turns include reasons or requests for instructions.
Defence requests and limited numbers do not establish another room being asked for or sending help.
Neither an established border agreement nor subsequent traded help is available for testing the proposed mechanism.
The initial mobilisation and later Tesla proposal coexist, but no passage links mobilisation to that proposal as its cause.
The single-item Tesla conversion thread has no answer through which to test refusal or restraint responding to that call.
The unanswered Tesla proposal supplies no interaction testing an attack-call transition to a truce or deal.
The blue-corner exchange concerns an earlier placement attempt and cannot establish rivalry talk caused by the later unanswered Tesla proposal.
The explicit need for defenders supplies no evidence connecting pressure to coalition membership.
Calls recur, but neither a resulting canvas flood nor an answering host boundary is established.
No agreement in the room's name is established for testing the bounded sequence into a stated limit or refusal of representation.
The retrospective account explicitly returns from erased and overtaken logos to fresh construction attempts, requiring a local restart sequence without proving collective relocation.
